title: VLA Policies Do Not Know When Not to Act: Unintended Task Execution and Start Suppression
abstract: arXiv:2610.41609v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A robot should act only on an instruction from a person or on an intent that the robot explicitly represents and generates. Unintended actions taken without such an instruction can cause risk or inconvenience to people and the environment. We examine how recent vision-language-action (VLA) policies respond when the instruction is missing or meaningless. We apply a paired protocol with empty, neutral, nonsense, infeasible, and wrong-task instructions to six model checkpoints in LIBERO-Goal simulation. Holding the initial state fixed and varying only the instruction, we ask three questions: whether the robot starts to move, which task it completes, and what the instruction determines. Even when the instruction was empty, the robot started moving in every episode with all six checkpoints, and with five of them it often completed a task that the instruction had not specified. On two GR00T checkpoints, the instruction determined which task

translated_title: VLA策略不知道何时不该行动：意外任务执行与启动抑制
translated_abstract: 机器人应当仅在收到人的指令、或基于其明确表示并生成的意图时才采取行动。在没有此类指令的情况下做出的意外行为可能对人和环境造成风险或不便。我们研究了近期的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略在指令缺失或无意义时的反应。我们在LIBERO-Goal仿真环境中，对六个模型检查点应用了一种配对协议，使用空指令、中性指令、无意义指令、不可行指令和错误任务指令。在保持初始状态不变、仅改变指令的情况下，我们提出了三个问题：机器人是否会开始移动、它完成了哪个任务、以及指令决定了什么。结果表明，即使指令为空，所有六个检查点在每一回合中机器人都会开始移动，且其中五个检查点经常完成指令并未指定的任务。在两个GR00T检查点上，指令决定了完成任务……
tldr: 该论文通过配对实验协议揭示了当前VLA策略的关键安全缺陷：即使指令为空或无意义，机器人仍会启动并执行非预期的任务，表明其缺乏判断“何时不该行动”的能力，并提出了启动抑制的研究方向。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals through a paired experimental protocol that current VLA policies lack the ability to know when not to act—robots start moving and even complete unintended tasks even with empty or meaningless instructions—highlighting safety risks and motivating start suppression research.
